system.name: RingLeader
system.one_liner: a system that offloads intra-server request scheduling and load balancing across services and cores to the NIC

components.name: Datapath OS
components.role: single-address-space host OS that multiplexes per-core coroutines for multiple services

components.name: Core 1
components.role: host core running a coroutine scheduler and per-core buffer for one or more services

components.name: Core 2
components.role: second host core with the same coroutine scheduler / per-core buffer structure

components.name: Core N
components.role: further host core with the same coroutine scheduler / per-core buffer structure

components.name: Coroutines Scheduler
components.role: per-core scheduler that launches the runnable coroutine for the highest-priority request

components.name: Per-core Buffer
components.role: per-core buffer holding requests awaiting a coroutine on that core

components.name: Core Allocator
components.role: reassigns cores across services as load changes

components.name: RMT Pipeline
components.role: programmable match+action pipeline that parses a packet's L3-L7 headers to identify its service and compute its rank

components.name: on-NIC Request Buffer
components.role: per-service packet buffer queue holding requests waiting to be scheduled

components.name: on-NIC Request Scheduler
components.role: schedules different services' requests with a first-eligible-out (FEO) policy

components.name: on-NIC Request Load Balancer
components.role: steers the scheduled service's request to an eligible core with the lowest rank using JBSRQ

per-service buffered requests waiting to be scheduled

content.key_idea: RingLeader offloads request scheduling and load balancing onto the NIC: an RMT pipeline classifies packets by service, an on-NIC scheduler (FEO) picks the highest-priority eligible service, and a load balancer (JBSRQ) steers it to the least-loaded core, whose coroutine scheduler runs it and feeds load status back.
content.reading_order: Bottom-up on the NIC: an incoming packet enters the RMT Pipeline, is buffered per service, scheduled, and load-balanced across cores; the top shows the resulting per-core coroutine scheduling on the Datapath OS host, with a Core Allocator reassigning cores across services.

summary: This figure shows RingLeader's whole-system architecture for offloading intra-server request scheduling and load balancing onto the NIC. On the host side, a Datapath OS runs identical Core 1...Core N structures, each with a Coroutines Scheduler and Per-core Buffer, alongside a Core Allocator that reassigns cores across services. Across a PCIe boundary, the NIC has an RMT Pipeline that parses packet headers to identify service and rank, an on-NIC Request Buffer queuing them per service, an on-NIC Request Scheduler using a first-eligible-out (FEO) policy guided by an eligibility mask, and an on-NIC Request Load Balancer that steers each request to the least-loaded eligible core via JBSRQ. Load Feedback, Scale up/down Hints, and Core Reallocation Events arrows close the loop between cores and NIC. Boxes use blue for NIC scheduling, red for coroutine/queue icons, green for the Core Allocator, and tan for the Load Monitor and RMT Pipeline.
summary_zh: 该图展示RingLeader整体架构：主机侧Datapath OS的多个核心运行协程调度器与核心分配器；网卡侧RMT流水线解析数据包，经请求缓冲、FEO调度器与JBSRQ负载均衡器分派至最优核心，并反馈负载信息。
notes: The direction of the 'Eligibility mask' arrow was inferred from the RingLeader Overview text (the scheduler/load-balancer interface 'expos[es] available room at per-core buffers to the scheduler') rather than from reading the arrowhead alone.
